results.name: SpaceX CRS-35 Dragon Docking

vid_urls.title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Rendezvous and Docking
vid_urls.description:
Following a successful launch on Oct. 13, 2026, an uncrewed SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft will plan to rendezvous with and dock to the International Space Station. The spacecraft, which is carrying over 6,300 pounds of supplies, is scheduled to dock autonomously at about 11 a.m. EDT (1500 UTC).

In addition to cargo for the crew aboard the space station, Dragon will deliver several new science experiments that could help restore vision for people on Earth with artificial eye retinas, develop more realistic heart tissue models for disease research, and identify new treatment targets for diseases like Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and multiple sclerosis.

Dragon is scheduled to remain at the space station for one month before undocking and splashing down off the coast of California.

After more than seven months aboard the International Space Station, NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles. The crew members will discuss their science mission during a news conference at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev will answer questions about their mission.

NASA will hold a media teleconference to preview the agency’s contributions to JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission. The mission is scheduled to launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan on Monday, Oct. 19 EDT (Tuesday, Oct. 20 JST).

Participants in the briefing, who will provide an overview of the mission and NASA’s contributions, include:
- Lindsay Hays, acting director, Planetary Science Division, NASA Headquarters in Washington
- Tom Statler, MMX program executive and scientist, Planetary Science Division, NASA Headquarters
- David Lawrence, MEGANE (Mars-moon Exploration with Gamma-rays and Neutrons) principal investigator, Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory
- Kris Zacny, vice president, Blue Origin’s Honeybee Robotics

info_urls.title: Solar Orbiter: journey around the Sun
info_urls.description: Solar Orbiter: journey around the Sun

results.description: Solar Orbiter, a partnership between ESA and NASA, will perform a gravity assist maneuver with Venus on December 24, 2026. Throughout its mission it also makes repeated gravity assist flybys of Venus to get closer to the Sun, and to change its orbital inclination, boosting it out of the ecliptic plane, to get the best – and first – views of the Sun’s poles.
